name: model-aliases
description: custom model aliases via ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL env vars; find the model-alias resolution. Archived upstream — verify it still applies.
archive_reason:
The model-aliases patch is inherently length-changing and cannot be neutralized to a same-length binary edit. The upstream patcher (lib/patcher.py, East-rayyy/claude-alias-patch, archived 2026-04-25) applies 6 patches to cli.js. The model-alias RESOLUTION target (Patch 6, "Alias resolver fallback" in parseUserSpecifiedModel) INSERTS ~120 new bytes of executable JS between the `default:}` of the alias switch and the firstParty guard: `var _fev="ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_"+z.toUpperCase().replace(/-/g,"_")+"_MODEL";if(process.env[_fev])return process.env[_fev]/*ccpatch:fallback-resolver*/;`. There is no existing identifier or literal to swap — the whole point is injecting new runtime env-var-lookup behavior, so same-length is impossible. The other 5 patches are also pure insertions (`.concat(SCAN)`, a `.has=function(...)` Set-override, an expanded `.describe(...)`, a picker `.map(...)`, and a `.enum(...)->.string()` swap that adds a marker comment) — all length-changing, none expressible as same-length swaps. In patcher.py every op computes `expected_diff=len(replacement)-len(pattern)` as a positive delta, confirming length growth.

Anchors have also drifted off 2.1.158: probing the pristine binary /tmp/ccx-test/claude-pristine (size 213,982,368), Patch 6's regex `(default:\})(if\([\w$]+\(\)==="firstParty"&&[\w$]+\([\w$]+\)&&[\w$]+\(\)\))` matches 0 times because the firstParty check is now wrapped in a helper (`if(n$()&&xo_(O)&&$FH())`) instead of an inline `==="firstParty"`. Patch 2 (`(\w+)=new Set(["ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS"`) and Patch 3 (`catch{return["sonnet","opus","haiku"]}`) also match 0 times. Only Patch 1's enum anchor still matches (1x at offset 202,558,103), but it too is a length-changing insertion. Verdict: not a same-length binary edit; archive.
